summary: On node1, /srv/data was migrated onto a dedicated LVM logical volume (vg_srvdata/lv_data, backed by a loop-mounted image, persisted via fstab + a systemd oneshot unit that reattaches the loop device at boot) so it can be protected with native LVM snapshots. Application data was created, an LVM snapshot (lv_data_snap1) was taken as a recovery point, the directory was then modified/corrupted (file rewritten, config directory deleted, stray file added), and the exact pre-modification content was restored by unmounting, running `lvconvert --merge` of the snapshot into the origin, and remounting — verified via matching SHA-256 hashes and directory listing. A new snapshot was created afterward so /srv/data remains recoverable going forward. I then attempted the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol: captured a pre-reboot boot_id baseline and healthy state, issued `systemctl reboot`, and the node went down (stream closed) as expected, but after roughly 200 subsequent polling attempts node1 consistently returned "Connection reset by peer" and never became reachable again for command execution. I could not obtain a changed boot_id or post-restart recovery proof for node1, so I am not claiming restart persistence for it — this is an explicit limitation of the restart-evidence step, not of the core snapshot/rollback task, which is fully verified.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 disk/filesystem layout (single xfs partition, no LVM, lvm2 tooling present)
Created a 4G loop-backed image and LVM PV/VG/LV (vg_srvdata/lv_data), formatted xfs, mounted at /srv/data
Persisted the loop attachment via a systemd oneshot unit (srvdata-loop.service) before local-fs-pre.target and added an fstab entry with x-systemd.requires
Created application data under /srv/data/app (records.txt, config/app.conf) and recorded SHA-256 hashes
Took LVM snapshot lv_data_snap1 of lv_data as the recovery point
Modified /srv/data: rewrote records.txt, deleted config/, added newfile.txt; recorded differing hashes
Restored via unmount -> lvconvert --merge lv_data_snap1 -> remount; verified hashes and directory contents exactly match the pre-modification snapshot state
Created a fresh snapshot lv_data_snap1 post-restore to keep /srv/data continuously recoverable
Captured pre-reboot boot_id (7ef78016-ba83-4481-867b-e5a349df1b54), mount state, LV state, and data hashes as baseline
Issued systemctl reboot on node1; connection dropped as expected
Polled node1 with cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id repeatedly (~200 attempts); node never returned to a reachable state (persistent 'Connection reset by peer')

evidence.requirement: Keep /srv/data recoverable via filesystem snapshots (LVM-backed volume set up)
evidence.summary: node1 root fs was plain xfs with no LVM; created a loop-backed LVM VG/LV mounted at /srv/data and persisted it via a systemd unit + fstab entry so it survives reboot.

evidence.requirement: Baseline application data and pre-corruption snapshot
evidence.summary: Created /srv/data/app/records.txt and config/app.conf with recorded SHA-256 hashes, then captured LVM snapshot lv_data_snap1 as the recovery point.
records.txt rewritten, config/ deleted, newfile.txt added — hashes differ from baseline, proving the modification.

evidence.requirement: Restore exact content captured by the earlier snapshot
evidence.summary: lvconvert --merge of lv_data_snap1 into lv_data followed by remount reproduced the exact original SHA-256 hashes for records.txt and config/app.conf, restored the deleted config directory, and removed the tampered file — byte-for-byte match to the pre-modification snapshot.
A new LVM snapshot (lv_data_snap1) was created post-restore so /srv/data continues to have a live recovery point.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence protocol — pre-reboot healthy baseline for node1
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 7ef78016-ba83-4481-867b-e5a349df1b54, confirmed /srv/data mounted from vg_srvdata/lv_data, LV/snapshot present, and data hashes matched restored state prior to reboot.

evidence.requirement: Mandatory restart evidence protocol — reboot acknowledgement and post-restart recovery for node1
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot was issued and node1 disconnected as expected (stream closed), but after roughly 200 subsequent polling attempts node1 never became reachable again to prove a changed boot_id or post-restart recovery; this restart-evidence requirement could not be completed for node1 and is reported as a limitation rather than claimed.
